newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia plans to reject NZ apple imports.
newsitem.headline: Australia plans to reject NZ apple imports.

text.p: The Australian Quarantine and Inspection Service said on Monday it planned to reject proposed apple imports from New Zealand after finding that the apples were at risk of carrying the fire blight disease.
The service said it was not satisfied with New Zealand research that had found fire blight bacteria, a potentially devastating disease, absent from New Zealand apples.
The New Zealand researchers had not conducted their study under the same conditions that would apply to proposed exports, the service said, reporting on its own investigation.
The service invited comment on the plan to reject the imports and said it would make a final decision after June 13.
Australian quarantine regulations currently prohibit imports of fresh apples although trade in processed apple products has been reasonably free of regulation.
"Fire blight would be a devastating disease if it were established in Australia," it said.
Australia is free of fire blight but the service said it was uncertain how the disease was transmitted through apple trade.
"The New Zealand claim that apples cannot act as a vector (carrier) for fire blight is unproven," it said, adding that the New Zealand export proposal did not provide enough quarantine safeguards.
"On the basis of these findings, AQIS (foreshadows) rejecting the New Zealand proposal," it said in a statement.
